body:
FILES, THE TRAP THE REGISTER'S FIX DOES NOT SAY, AND THE TESTS (code read 6 Nov 2026, main 068c71a; B-61 has the run).

WHERE: `applyPlaylists` (app/lib/data/encore/encore_writer.dart:153-215) writes the server's name, cover and `deletedAtMs: null` for every playlist row of the feed and replaces its entries, then `_renumber`. The protection that exists, `pendingStarTargets` (data/sync/pending_intent.dart:13), looks only at outbox kinds `star`/`unstar` and the payload keys `songIds`, `albumIds`, `artistIds`. The playlist kinds (outbox.dart:32-40) are `playlist.create`, `playlist.update` (payload `playlistId`, `name?`, `add[]`, `removeIdx[]`, `removeIds[]`) and `playlist.delete` (payload `id`). So the new set is the `playlistId`/`id` of pending rows of those kinds, read the same way (status `pending` only: a parked, failed edit lets the server's truth show, as for likes).

THE TRAP. The feed is a cursor (encore_sync.dart:101, the cursor is stored after each page). If the pull SKIPS a playlist because an edit of it waits, the cursor still moves past that row. The other device's change (in the B-61 run: a song added) is then never sent to this phone again, because the row is only repeated when the thing is touched again. Skipping alone replaces "the name flicks back" by "the other device's song never arrives". The fix therefore has two halves: (1) skip the writes for a playlist with a waiting edit, and (2) remember the playlist as stale and read it again once the edit is delivered or parked. The phone has no call for one playlist today (`GET playlists/{pl}` exists on the server, docs/17; `EncoreApi` has none), so either add that call or reset the playlists' cursor for that id. The alternative, per field (keep the waiting name and merge the entries), is harder: entries removed locally would come back, so the whole playlist is the right unit.

KEEP CF-21: a playlist DELETED on the server wins over a waiting edit of it (docs/34 CF-21, "delete wins, silently"). So the protection applies to the non-deleted branch only; the tombstone branch (encore_writer.dart:162-171) keeps working.

TESTS: the rule has its test for likes only: test/data/encore/encore_sync_test.dart:214 ('a like that is still waiting in the outbox is not undone by what the server last knew'; its outbox insert at 221 is the pattern). Add: a rename waits, the feed brings the old name: the screen keeps the new one; the same for a delete and for removed entries; and the new one the trap needs: the feed carries another device's added song while the rename waits, the edit is delivered, the song is there. Update docs/34 rule 5 (line 17) from "a like or unlike" to every kind of waiting edit, and its test column.
